summary: This area is in better shape than its risk profile suggests. I checked every Metal parameter-struct pair byte-for-byte — CubeDims (16 B), ApertureParams (32 B), CoMParams (28 B), OriginParams (24 B) in MetalEngine.swift:26-66 against DPStatistics.metal:17-22 / VirtualDiffraction.metal:19-24 / VirtualMask.metal:16-21 / VirtualAperture.metal:16-25 / CenterOfMass.metal:18-26 / OriginMeasure.metal:21-28, plus the out-of-file ACOMMetalParams (OrientationMatcher.swift:329-334) against ACOMMatching.metal:4-9 — all field orders, types and sizes match, every field is 4 bytes, and every kernel's declared buffer index is bound. Other things done well: the resident-cube `cubeOffset` path re-asserts its own bounds against `cube.buffer.length` (VirtualDetector.swift:153-156) rather than trusting the caller; the vDSP 2D FFT's argument order AND its inverse normalization are genuinely pinned by a *non-square, power-of-two* py4DSTEM parity fixture (32x64, tools/disk-detection-test/reference.py:52, absolute intensities to 2e-4), so a log2n0/log2n1 swap or a double-scaled inverse cannot pass; the exact radix-3/5 FFT is pinned by analytic bin values, not just a round trip that two inverse mistakes could satisfy (tools/disk-detection-test/main.swift:220-255); the ACOM Metal path is mathematically identical to the CPU oracle including the conjugation sign and the lowest-index tie-break (ACOMMatching.metal:38-39,72-86 vs OrientationMatcher.swift:165-206), and its init guards azimuthal to a power of two <= maxTotalThreadsPerThreadgroup (OrientationMatcher.swift:362-368) so the threadgroup barrier can never be reached divergently. The four findings below are all deviations from py4DSTEM that no harness can currently see. Known items I deliberately did not re-report: the uncancellable single `waitUntilCompleted` (open-items #37, lines ~2098-2110), the coarse bin grid starting at pixel (0,0) (~line 1712), and the unpinned mask-boundary convention generally (~line 1818). One latent trap worth a comment, not a finding: acomInverseArgmax's `threadIndex >= params.azimuthal` early return (ACOMMatching.metal:62-63) sits before a threadgroup_barrier, so it is only safe because the dispatch sets threadgroup width exactly equal to nAzimuthal; any future rounding of the threadgroup size to threadExecutionWidth would make that barrier divergent (undefined behaviour / hang).

findings.title: DFT-upsample kernel uses the wrong Fourier frequency for one bin when width or height is odd
findings.why: py4DSTEM's dftUpsample builds its kernel frequencies as `np.fft.ifftshift(np.arange(n)) - np.floor(n/2)` (References/py4DSTEM-dev/py4DSTEM/process/utils/multicorr.py:186 for columns, :195 for rows), which for n=7 gives [0,1,2,3,-3,-2,-1]. The Swift port hand-rolls this as `frequencyColumn < width/2 ? fc : fc - width` (MatrixDFTCorrelation.swift:143-146) and the identical expression for rows (:168-171). Integer division makes the test `fc < (n-1)/2` for odd n, so the bin at index (n-1)/2 is assigned frequency (n-1)/2 - n instead of +(n-1)/2 — off by exactly n. Even n is correct; odd n has exactly one wrong bin out of n. The repo already owns a correct helper for this exact mapping, `FFT2D.fftfreq` (FFT2D.swift:465-467, `k <= (n-1)/2`), which parallax and ptychography use (ParallaxAberrationCorrection.swift:91, PtychographyPreparation.swift:152) — so the two conventions disagree inside one module. No harness can see it: the disk-detection parity fixture is 32x64 (tools/disk-detection-test/reference.py:52) and the parallax-alignment fixture is 12x16 (tools/parallax-alignment-test/reference.py:44-46), both even on both axes, and the parallax reference.py:196-199 implements the *correct* ifftshift form, so it would catch this the moment a fixture dimension were odd.
findings.failureScenario: A 101x101 scan run through parallax: ParallaxPreprocessing.swift:290 makes stackHeight = 101 + 32 = 133 (odd), ParallaxAlignment.swift:282 builds FFT2D(nx:.., ny:133), and correlationShift -> MatrixDFTCorrelation.refinedPeak (ParallaxAlignment.swift:483) upsamples with row frequency index 66 carrying phase for -67 cycles instead of +66. The row kernel is wrong for that component, the upsampled patch is wrong, and every per-plane BF shift — and therefore the reconstructed aberration fit — is systematically biased. Same for disk detection (DiskDetection.swift:736) on any odd-sized detector or crop.

findings.title: CoM kernels clamp negative pixels to zero — an unnoted py4DSTEM deviation
findings.why: Both center-of-mass kernels apply `max(pat[...], 0.0f)` before accumulating (CenterOfMass.metal:53 and OriginMeasure.metal:85). py4DSTEM does not: get_CoM sums the array as given (References/py4DSTEM-dev/py4DSTEM/process/utils/utils.py:184-186), and the phase/DPC CoM sums raw intensities with no clip (References/py4DSTEM-dev/py4DSTEM/process/phase/phase_base_class.py:694-703). The repo's hard rule is that port deviations carry an inline DEVIATION note with the reason; the only DEVIATION note in this whole area is OriginMeasure.metal:7-15, which covers the coarse binning step and says nothing about clamping. Grep confirms no other DEVIATION note and no mention of the clamp anywhere in docs/. This matters because the clamp is not neutral: it changes both the numerator and the denominator of the CoM whenever the data carries negatives.
findings.failureScenario: A dark-reference-subtracted or gain-corrected DM4/HDF5 cube whose background pixels sit slightly below zero: py4DSTEM's CoM lets those negatives cancel background asymmetry, the app's CoM discards them, so the DPC shift field and the measured origin map differ from py4DSTEM by a background-dependent offset. Because the offset varies smoothly with the background, it survives the rotation fit as a real-looking rotation/strain bias rather than as noise, and a reader comparing the app's DPC to py4DSTEM's on the same file has no note anywhere telling them why the numbers differ.

findings.title: Origin CoM window includes its boundary ring; py4DSTEM's is strictly inside
findings.why: py4DSTEM's get_origin masks with `np.hypot(qxx-_qx0, qyy-_qy0) < r*rscale` — strictly less than (References/py4DSTEM-dev/py4DSTEM/process/calibration/origin.py:214, and again at :290 and :318 for the datacube loop). The kernel implements the complement as `if (dx*dx + dy2 > win2) { continue; }` (OriginMeasure.metal:84, and :80 for the row pre-test), which admits pixels at exactly dist^2 == win2, i.e. `<=`. Exact equality is reachable, not a float-tie curiosity: `bin = round(r)` (line 42), so an odd bin puts the winning block centre on an integer (0.5*(bx+xEnd-1) with bin=5 gives 2.0), dx and dy are then integers, and a typical r=5, rscale=1.2 gives win2 = 36.0 exactly — every on-axis pixel 6 px out is included by the app and excluded by py4DSTEM. The 2026-08-19 Gate B finding recorded in docs/open-items.md (~line 1818) says exactly this class of change is invisible to the current harnesses because both sides run the same mask code; the S11 bounds-convention sweep (~line 313) audited the annulus predicate and the coarse seed but not this window.
findings.failureScenario: A cube with probe radius ~5 px calibrated with the default rscale=1.2: the CoM refinement window carries an extra ring of boundary pixels relative to py4DSTEM. Where the ring is asymmetrically illuminated (a nearby Bragg disk on one side), the measured origin shifts sub-pixel in that direction, propagating into Q calibration and the strain map, with no harness able to flag the difference.

findings.title: A zero-intensity pattern silently reports an exactly zero DPC shift
findings.why: When the clamped pattern sum is not positive, the kernel sets comX/comY to the reference centre (CenterOfMass.metal:60-61), so the emitted vector at :63-64 is exactly (0, 0) — indistinguishable from a scan position whose beam is perfectly centred. py4DSTEM divides by the raw sum (phase_base_class.py:694-703, utils.py:184-186) and therefore yields NaN/inf, which propagates visibly and which get_origin even has an explicit `remove_NaN` path for. The app's consumer cannot tell the two apart: computeCoMField (App/AppState.swift:4253-4275) returns a plain [Float] with no validity mask, and the field feeds both the R-Q rotation fit and iDPC integration.
findings.failureScenario: A scan region where the beam is blanked or the detector drops out for some rows (or a detector crop that excludes all signal for part of the scan): those positions contribute hard (0,0) vectors to the rotation fit and to the iDPC integration instead of being excluded or flagged, pulling the fitted rotation angle toward zero shift and putting a flat, real-looking patch into the integrated phase map.
